clue.text: Colour scheme in main gaol

indicators.note: to scheme is to plot or contrive, so the letters of the next two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A prison's decorating plan for its main block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheme' looks like part of 'Colour scheme', but it is the anagram signal working on MAIN GAOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolia is a pale creamy-white shade much used for interior walls, named after the flower.

clue.text: A horse welcomes middle age spread!

indicators.note: a host welcomes a guest inside, so one piece is placed within another here

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: the word middle asks for the centre letter of the word age

explanation.surface: Joking that a horse is happy to put on weight in midlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle age spread' reads as one phrase about weight gain; it splits into G (middle of 'age') and the definition 'spread'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marge is the informal British name for margarine, a butter substitute one spreads on bread.

clue.text: Ill-reputed refusal to start repaying debts

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here taken from repaying

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A debtor who will not even begin paying back what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, so having a poor reputation.

clue.text: Affair gives rise to trouble with one offspring

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from bottom to top, so it is written backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a child, offspring

explanation.surface: An extramarital affair leads to problems once a child arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns AIL into LIA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic relationship, a love affair.

clue.text: Broadcasting covers state of cooling equipment

indicators.note: one piece covers another by going round it, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: airing a programme is broadcasting it
a condition is a state something is in

explanation.surface: A TV report on how bad the cooling system is.
explanation.definitionFit: This system chills the air in a building, a kind of cooling apparatus.

clue.text: Sailor's view listened to by setter, perhaps

indicators.note: what is listened to is heard rather than read, so a word is swapped for one sounding the same

parts.note: to see is to view
a setter is one breed of dog, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A sailor's opinion is heard by the crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' seems to mean the crossword compiler, but here it is the gun dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, experienced mariner is informally called this.

clue.text: Alternative theatre's outside facility for keeping stock

indicators.note: one piece sits outside another, so the second goes within the first

parts.note: the stage stands for theatre as a profession
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A fringe theatre company's external warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot or warehouse provides space where goods are kept until needed.

clue.text: Is comfort to follow Germany's sickness?

indicators.note: these words place the later pieces after the letter for Germany

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
ease is comfort

explanation.surface: Asking whether solace after German rule is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease is an illness or disorder of the body.

clue.text: Pledge to (almost) defend worker on drugs

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: to guard is to defend
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker
E stands for the drug ecstasy, doubled here for the plural

explanation.surface: Promising to protect, more or less, an employee who uses drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal promise or assurance.

clue.text: Performing arts, or platforms for them?

indicators.note: to perform a piece is to work it over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether performing arts need stages to be shown on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing arts' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'Performing' is the anagram signal for ARTS OR; 'for them' ties the platforms to the performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostra is the plural of rostrum, a raised stand or dais for a speaker.

clue.text: Old country ways rumoured to get first class backing

indicators.note: what is rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is replaced by one sounding like it

parts.note: roads are ways

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Traditional customs, said to be getting top-class support.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of the African state now called Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Coffee and English Sunday papers love?

parts.note: the press means the newspapers
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A coffee and the English Sunday newspapers make for a cosy morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: All pay can be docked — that's material

indicators.note: a tail that is docked is cut short, so each of these words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Every wage can be cut, and that is what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be docked' trims the final letter from each of ALL, PAY and CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is a fine woollen fabric woven from the fleece of the Andean animal.

clue.text: Pig ate outside, ignored

indicators.note: one piece eats round another, so the second goes within the first

parts.note: dined means ate
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pig eating outdoors was overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disowned is to be rejected or repudiated, shunned by those who should own you.

clue.text: The disadvantages are an attraction to defenders

parts.note: a draw is something that attracts people
backs are defending players in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A team's weak points prove appealing to its defensive players.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawbacks are snags or downsides.

clue.text: Once through time, become skilled

parts.note: ex means once, former
per means through, by way of

explanation.surface: Over time, someone develops real ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is a link word; 'skilled' alone is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert person is highly proficient, adept.

clue.text: A dog always welcomes favourite

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'A dog always welcomes favourite (9)': PUP + EER around PET makes the letters, but no word is left to define the answer; the definition seems cut off and a search did not find the full clue.

clue.text: Tickled by a thought

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: Someone tickled pink by an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tickled is to be entertained or diverted.

clue.text: A French comic lacks humour

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the adjective, as in a joke that lacks humour

parts.note: un is French for a
funny means comic

explanation.surface: A French comedian who is not at all amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase, read as 'is humourless' for the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unamusing is without wit, not at all comic.

clue.text: Presents a note, accepted by mafia bosses

indicators.note: what is accepted by a piece is taken inside it

parts.note: dons are Mafia chiefs
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Gifts and a message are received by crime lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Donates means gives, as a gift or present.

clue.text: Go and fish where a charge is levied

parts.note: a turn is a go in a game
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Take your turn and go fishing at a spot that charges a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is a road with tolls, where drivers pay to pass.

clue.text: Case of rosé before the wedding party

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: a union is a marriage or wedding

explanation.surface: A box of rosé is brought out ahead of the wedding party.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion is a gathering of old friends or family, a social get-together.

clue.text: Scientist in second class cricket side batting

parts.note: B denotes second class
the off side is one half of a cricket field
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A researcher playing for a lower-grade cricket team, now in to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's field is split into the off side and the leg side; the batting team is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.

clue.text: Leonard rode in new coupé — what luxury!

indicators.note: someone who rode in a car sat inside it, so this piece goes within the other
new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Len is short for Leonard

explanation.surface: Leonard took a ride in a brand-new sports car, and how plush it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leonard rode in new coupé' reads as a story about a car; 'new' is the anagram signal and 'rode in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth and lavishness, sumptuous living.

clue.text: Cancel prior to accepting a second

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the next pieces go inside

parts.note: ere means before, prior to

explanation.surface: Calling something off before agreeing to a follow-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete.

clue.text: It may be scattered to infect bride and groom

definitions.text: It may be scattered to infect bride and groom

indicators.note: letters that are scattered are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Something thrown over newlyweds that might pass on germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges TO INFECT, while the whole clue describes what guests throw at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper confetti is thrown over a newly married couple as they leave the ceremony.

clue.text: Where one manufactures brie — Austria?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to manufacture is to make something new, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: Asking whether the French cheese is really made in Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactures' rearranges BRIE into BERI. The question mark admits the whole clue is a playful riddle: the place asked for is a peninsula, not Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, a place answering the question 'where'.

clue.text: Hasty lessons in revealing fashions

indicators.note: the words show what lies in them, so the letters are taken from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Quick classes on how to wear daring clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealing fashions' suggests skimpy clothes, but 'in revealing' signals the run inside 'Hasty lessons'.
explanation.definitionFit: Styles are modes of dress, trends.

clue.text: Produce information and point to charge

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E is a compass point, east
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Producing data and suggesting a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to create or bring about.
